task:
Add a nullish coalescing operator, x ?? y, to the expression parser, backed by a new function math.nullish(x, y). It returns y when x is null or undefined, and x otherwise. 0, false, '', NaN and zero values of Complex, BigNumber, Fraction and Unit are not nullish, and the same object comes back.

The operator

- It parses to an OperatorNode with op '??' and fn 'nullish'. getOperator('nullish') returns '??'. It is left-associative, so null ?? undefined ?? 42 is 42 and 5 ?? null ?? 42 is 5.
- Its precedence is unusual on purpose. It binds tighter than every binary operator, including ^ and .^, but looser than the postfix operators ! and '. So 1 + null ?? 2 is 3, 2 * null ?? 3 is 6, 2 ^ null ?? 3 is 8, 2 .^ null ?? 3 is 8, 5 ?? 2 ^ 3 is 125, 3 ^ null ?? 2 ^ 2 is 81, false ?? 3 ^ 2 is 0, 5! ?? 2 is 120, null ?? 3! is 6, and (null ?? 3)! is 6. It also binds tighter than and, or, xor and the conditional: null ?? false or true is true, true xor null ?? 42 is false, 5 ?? null ? 1 : 2 is 1, null ?? 0 ? 1 : 2 is 2. With parentheses, (1 + null) ?? 2 throws TypeError: Unexpected type of argument.
- In the precedence table used by getPrecedence with parenthesis 'keep', the ?? operator has level 17, between exponentiation and factorial. Logical or stays at 2, and the transpose in parse("M'") moves to 19. getAssociativity gives 'left'.
- In an expression it short-circuits. When the left value is not a collection and not null or undefined, the right side is not evaluated at all. When the left side is null or undefined, the right side is evaluated once. When the left side is a matrix or array, the right side is evaluated once and the element-wise rules below apply. An undefined symbol on the left still throws Undefined symbol x; it is not treated as nullish. nullish(x, 42) as a function call in an expression gives the same results.

The function, for collections

- A scalar left value that is not nullish is returned as is, even with a matrix on the right. A null or undefined left value returns the right value, the same object.
- A collection on the left with a scalar on the right works element-wise: nullish([null, undefined], 42) is [42, 42], and a dense matrix [[null, 0], [undefined, 1]] with 42 gives [[42, 0], [42, 1]].
- Two collections work element-wise with no broadcasting, so the shapes must match exactly, in any number of dimensions. Mismatched dense or array shapes throw a RangeError whose message contains Dimension mismatch, for example nullish([1], [7, 8]).
- A sparse matrix on the left is returned unchanged when the right side has exactly the same size, whether the right side is an array, a dense matrix or a sparse matrix. When the sizes differ, it throws a DimensionError, whose message contains Dimension mismatch.
- A dense matrix on the left with a sparse matrix on the right works element-wise: [[null, 1]] with sparse [[10, 20]] gives [[10, 1]].
- Result types: Array with Array gives an Array. Array with a dense matrix, and a dense matrix with an Array, give a Matrix. Array with a scalar gives an Array. In math.evaluate, array literals are matrices, so [null, 5] ?? [1, 2] gives matrix([1, 5]), and [] ?? [7, 8] throws a RangeError.

Register nullish in the default instance so math.nullish exists, give it embedded docs like the other functions, and list the operator in the syntax docs.

Everything else must keep working.
